shiftNote: This page shows a shift that starts at 7:00 AM. Recording starts at 8:00 AM. Other shifts follow the same order of steps.

day.what: Clock in and hand out the phones
day.text: The operators open the device room. They count the phones. They check the battery, the login, and the upload on every phone. Then they hand each phone to its wearer.
Recording runs in 30-minute cycles until 4:00 PM. The wearer does the task. The operator restarts every phone at the end of each cycle.
At every reset, the operator looks at the footage that was just recorded. If something is wrong, the operator fixes it right there.

day.what: Clock out and take the phones back
day.text: Every phone comes back. The operator takes it back by device number, inspects it, counts it, and puts it on a charger.

The Portfolio Manager looks at everything the site recorded today. The Portfolio Manager removes anything that should not be sent out. Then the Portfolio Manager sends the day's report to Mano by 6:00 PM. The report has the hours, the active phones, the hardware, the problems, and the fixes.
Anyone who cannot come to tomorrow's shift must call and message their Portfolio Manager by 8:00 PM tonight.

day.what: The hub run and the upload
day.text: The phones go to the closest hub. The runner takes one third of the phones on each run. At the hub, the phones upload over fiber during the night.
Two reviewers on the quality control team watch every video. If one of them says delete, the video is deleted.

rhythm: Friday is the day off in Egypt. Hotels keep running on Friday. They upload on their own internet lines.
Thursday is the day before the day off. On Thursday, every phone is flushed. Factory phones go to a hub for the night.

Once a week, on the same day each week, the Portfolio Manager compares three numbers: the number in the registry, the number in the MDM, and the number of phones in the device room. If the numbers are different, the Portfolio Manager checks why the same day.
Once a week, each Portfolio Manager's book is compared with its target.
In the last week of the month, Youssef Medhat runs the audit. Footage with a flag is deleted.
After the audit, we send the invoice. The invoice counts only the accepted hours. Everyone is paid based on that same number of hours.
always: If you cannot come tomorrow, call and message your Portfolio Manager by 8 PM tonight. If you do not, it counts as a no-show.
Each person has one account. Never share your account. Never use an old account again.
If a worker gets three flags, the worker comes off the phone. If the client gives a second strike, the phone is paused until the worker is trained again.
Never say the client's name to anyone, for any reason.

phases.title: Morning: the phones go out
phases.note: Clock-in is at 7:00 AM. There is one operator for every ten phones. The operators take the phones out of the device room.

phases.title: During the shift
phases.note: Recording runs from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM in 30-minute cycles. The operator checks the footage at every reset.

phases.title: Shift end: the phones come back
phases.note: The shift ends at 4:00 PM. Every phone comes back. The Portfolio Manager reviews the day before any footage uploads.

phases.title: Night: the hub run
phases.note: The phones go to the closest hub, one third at a time. They upload over fiber. Then two reviewers watch every video.

phases.title: Before the next shift
phases.note: The phones come back before the operators clock in. They are cleared and charged.

steps.title: Open the device room
steps.done: The room is open at 7:00 AM. Every phone is still on its charger. The phones were put there when they came back from the hub this morning.
lines: Open the device room at 7:00 AM. This room is the pickup location. The phones stay here, on their chargers. They do not stay anywhere else.
Keep the key with you. Nobody from the site opens this room. Nobody takes a phone off a charger before the count.
Call the operators into the room. There is one operator for every ten phones. The wearers wait at the pickup point outside the room. They wait until an operator calls their name.
The first cycle starts at 8:00 AM. The hour from 7:00 AM to 8:00 AM is for the checks below. Come early.

steps.title: Count the phones and write down the number
steps.done: The number you wrote on the count sheet is the number the site should have. If it is not, the Portfolio Manager already knows.
lines: Count every phone on the chargers. Count the spares too.
Write the number on the count sheet. Write the time and your name next to it. The sheet stays in the device room.
Compare the number with the manifest. The runner brought the manifest back this morning. The two numbers must be the same. If they are not the same, a phone is missing.
If a phone is missing at 7:00 AM, tell the Portfolio Manager now. Do not wait until the end of the shift. If nobody can find the phone, lost mode starts within one hour.

steps.title: Check every battery and login
steps.done: Every phone is charged. The collection app is open on every phone. Every phone is logged into its wearer's own account.
lines: Pick up each phone and look at the battery level. If a phone did not charge, put it back on the charger. A spare takes its place today.
Open the collection app on each phone. Check the account on the phone. The account must belong to the wearer who will carry the phone today. It must be in the wearer's own name.
Never let a wearer log into another person's account, not even for one cycle. If two people share an account, one person's fraud goes on the other person's name.
If a phone is on the wrong account, or the login does not work, take the phone to the Portfolio Manager. Do this before the phone goes on anyone's head.

steps.title: Check that last night's upload finished
steps.done: Every phone shows zero pending uploads in the collection app.
lines: Open the collection app on each phone. Look at the pending uploads. The number must be zero.
The hub attendant already checked this on the dashboard before the phones left the hub. Check it again here anyway.
If a phone still has yesterday's footage on it, it does not go on anyone's head. Put it aside. Tell the Portfolio Manager within the same hour.

Footage that is still on a phone at clock-in is called backlog. The Portfolio Manager counts backlog in device-days. If a site has more than one device-day of backlog, that is an incident. Moharam hears about it the same day.

steps.title: Hand each phone to its wearer
steps.done: Every phone that left the room has a row in the wearer log. The row has the wearer's name and the device number.
lines: Call the wearer by name. Only a wearer who passed onboarding screening gets a phone. This means four things: we have a copy of their ID on file, they signed the consent form, they signed off on the fraud briefing, and they have one account in their own name. If there is no file, there is no phone. It does not matter who at the site sent them.
Hand over the phone by its device number. Write a row in the wearer log with the wearer's name, the device number, the site, and the date.
Hand over the cap and the mount with the phone. Every wearer gets their own rig.
If a wearer looks under 18, or has no ID, do not give them a phone. Tell the Portfolio Manager now.

steps.title: Fit the rig and set the angle
steps.done: Every wearer has the cap on. The mount is tight. The camera sees what the wearer's eyes see.
lines: Put the cap on the wearer. Make the mount tight. Put the phone in the mount so it cannot slip. If the site needs a helmet, put the mount on the certified helmet. Do not change the helmet.

Set the camera angle. The camera must show what the wearer sees, with their hands and the work in the frame. It must not show the wearer's body or the floor. Do not use a chest strap. The client's system counts a chest mount as fraud, even if it is more comfortable.
While you fit the rig, say this rule again: before you take the hat off, tap stop. First press the button, then take off the hat.
Check that the wearer is wearing the site's safety gear before they walk to the floor. If any PPE is missing, they do not film until they put it on.
If the wearer works high up, attach a tether to the phone. If a phone falls from a height, that is an incident.

steps.title: Start the first cycle at 8:00 AM
steps.who: The wearer, watched by the operator
steps.done: Every phone on the floor is recording by 8:00 AM. Every camera angle is correct.
lines: At 8:00 AM, the wearer taps start and begins the assigned task. The wearer does not start before 8:00 AM. The hour from 7:00 AM to 8:00 AM is for the checks.
Walk around the floor in the first few minutes. Look at each phone. Check that it is recording, that the angle is right, and that the wearer is working.
While the cycle runs, the wearer does the task without stopping. The wearer does not use a personal phone, does not make calls, does not chat, and does not take breaks while the camera is recording.
If a wearer has no work to do, the wearer taps stop, tells you, and takes the rig off. Footage of a person doing nothing is fraud.

steps.title: Reset and check every 30 minutes
steps.done: Every phone was restarted on time. Before each new cycle began, the operator checked the footage from the last cycle. The footage looked right.
lines: The phone buzzes at the end of the cycle. That is your signal. Restart every phone the way the procedure says. Then walk the floor and check every restart yourself. This is the backup.

At every reset, look at the footage that was just recorded. Check the angle, the lighting, and that the wearer is still working. Fix problems right there. Fit the rig again, set the angle again, or remind the wearer of the rules.
At the same time, look at the storage and the battery on each phone. If a phone shows a storage warning, put a spare in its place now. That phone is flushed first tonight.
If a wearer does not follow the cycle, take the wearer off the phone. Tell the Portfolio Manager. A wearer who does not follow the rules during a cycle is removed from the site.
One operator can check ten phones every 30 minutes. If one operator has more than ten phones, restarts happen late and the number of flags goes up.

steps.title: The Portfolio Manager visits the site
steps.done: The Portfolio Manager visited the site today at a time nobody expected. The wrap report tonight will say what the Portfolio Manager found.
lines: Do not tell the site you are coming. Come at a different time each day. In the first week after launch, visit two or three times a day. In the second week, visit one or two times a day. After that, visit at least once a day.
Check the camera angles. Check that the 30-minute cycle is running. Check the chargers. Check the custody rows in the wearer log. Check how the wearers are doing.

Read every flag on the same day it arrives. Within 24 hours, go to the worker on the floor. Show them the video. Tell them one specific thing to correct. Then watch their next cycle to see that they fixed it.
Write what you found and what you fixed in the wrap report tonight.

steps.title: A phone stops working during the shift
steps.who: The operator first, then the Portfolio Manager
steps.done: The wearer is recording again on a spare phone. The spare is on the wearer's own account. The swap is written down.
lines: Tap stop. Take the rig off the wearer's head. Do not let a wearer keep working with a phone that is not recording. Those minutes do not count, whether the wearer keeps working or not.
Check the simple things first. Is the app open? Is the wearer on their own account? Is the recording running? Check the battery. Check the storage.
If the problem is the phone, give the wearer a spare right away. The wearer logs into their own account on the spare. The cycle restarts. The site never waits for a repair.

Write the swap in the wearer log. Tell the Portfolio Manager the device number, what broke, and whether there is still footage on the phone. Every transfer of a phone is written in the registry the same day.

The broken phone goes back to the device room. Leave its footage on it. If the phone can still upload, it goes to the hub tonight. Broken phones go to one repair shop once a week, all together. If the same part keeps breaking on many phones, tell Ali. Send Ali photos and the number of phones.

steps.title: Collect every phone at the end of the shift
steps.done: Every phone that went out this morning is back with the operator. The operator checked each device number against the wearer log.
lines: The last cycle ends at 4:00 PM. The wearer taps stop first. Then the wearer takes the hat off and brings the whole rig to the operator.
Take each phone back by its device number. Tick the wearer's row in the wearer log. The cap and the mount come back with the phone.
Count the rigs as they come in. Compare the count with the rows from this morning.

If a phone is not returned, tell the Portfolio Manager before anyone goes home. A phone can only be at the site, at a hub, or in a case that someone signed for. A phone anywhere else is a missing phone. Lost mode starts within one hour.

steps.title: Inspect and count again
steps.who: The operators, checked by the Portfolio Manager
steps.done: Every phone has a condition tick. The evening count matches the morning count.
lines: Check the condition of every phone: the screen, the port, the mount, and the battery. Tick each one. Write it next to the device number.
If the screen is cracked, the port is bad, or the mount is loose, a spare goes in for tomorrow. Write the damaged phone in the log for the weekly repair batch.
Count the phones again. Write the number on the count sheet, with the time and your name. The number must match the morning number.
The Portfolio Manager checks the count and the ticks before clocking out. If the number does not match, the Portfolio Manager must solve it tonight, not tomorrow.

steps.title: Put the phones on the chargers and check storage
steps.done: Every phone is on a charger in the device room. Every phone with a storage warning is marked on tonight's manifest.
lines: Put every phone on a charger in the device room. The kit has two multi-port chargers and one power strip for every ten phones. Lay the cables so nobody trips over them.
Look at the storage on every phone as you put it on the charger. If a phone has a storage warning, mark it. That phone is flushed first at the hub tonight.
Lock the room. The phones stay in the room until two things happen: the Portfolio Manager finishes reviewing the day, and the runner arrives.
No phone keeps more than one day of footage overnight. At a site that uses a hub, the upload happens at the hub, not at the site. This is why the hub run must never be late.

steps.title: The Portfolio Manager reviews the day
steps.done: The Portfolio Manager has looked at everything the site recorded today. Anything that should not go out has been removed. Mano has the wrap report by 6:00 PM.
lines: At 5:00 PM, look at everything the site recorded today, one phone at a time. Do this before any of it uploads. This is the second quality check. The operator's check at each reset was the first.
Remove anything that should not go out. Examples: a restroom, a screen, an ID document, a person under 18, or a rig worn on the chest. Write down the session, the device number, and the wearer.

Send the wrap report to Mano by 6:00 PM. The report has: the hours, the active phones, the hardware status, the problems, the fixes that other sites should copy, the backlog in device-days, and the day's rows from the wearer log.
Then give the phones to the runner. No phone leaves for the hub before this review is done.

steps.title: Pack one third of the phones for each run
steps.who: The operators, the runner, and the Portfolio Manager
steps.done: The runner has signed for one case. The manifest inside the case lists every phone in it.
lines: Never put more than one third of the site's phones in one case, one vehicle, or one run. If the site has 30 phones, that means three runs of ten phones. If the site has more than 60 phones, use two runners, and their runs leave at different times.

Use a hard case with a lock and no markings on it. Put the printed manifest inside the case. The manifest lists the device IDs, the count, the site, the time the case left, and the runner's name. On the manifest, mark the phones that must be flushed first.
The runner counts the phones and compares the count with the manifest. The runner does this before signing. Count first, then sign. Without a signature, there is no handover.

The Portfolio Manager signs the phones out to the runner. If the Portfolio Manager has already left, the senior operator signs instead. The person who hands over the phones signs, and the runner signs. Those two signatures are the custody record at pickup. MDM location tracking is on for every phone in the case.
The first run leaves as soon as the Portfolio Manager finishes the review. The last run must arrive at the hub before 11 PM.

steps.title: Drive straight to the closest hub
steps.done: Every case is at the hub and someone signed for it. The runner did not stop anywhere between the site and the hub.
lines: Take the case to the hub closest to the site. The hubs are the central hub downtown, Sheikh Zayed, and the Fifth Settlement. The site plan says which hub to use.

Carry the letter kit in your bag. The kit has four things: the company letter in Arabic on letterhead, a copy of the commercial register, the device list, and two phone numbers where someone will answer.
Never stop on the way. Never take phones home. Phones stay at the site, at a hub, or in a case that someone signed for. They stay nowhere else.
At a checkpoint, hand over the letter, the register, and the manifest. Then call Moharam. Never argue. Never hide the number of phones.
Go back to the site for the next third of the phones. There are no runs after 11 PM. So the first run must leave early enough for the last run to reach the hub before 11 PM.

steps.title: At the hub: count, sign, and charge
steps.done: Every phone on the manifest is counted and signed for. Every phone is on a charger and uploading.
lines: Take each case and open its manifest. Count the phones and compare the count with the manifest. The runner signs, and you sign. Those two signatures are the custody record at the hub.
Put every phone on a charger. Check that the collection app is uploading over the hub's fiber line. Phones that are marked to be flushed first go on first.
If a phone will not upload, hold it at the hub. Write in the log that you held it.

Write the night's numbers in the log: how many TB were uploaded, how many devices were cleared, and how many devices were held. If the hub is over 70% of its capacity for two nights, the search for the next hub starts.
If the hub's internet line goes down, call Mano. Moharam sends the remaining runs to the second hub within the same hour.

steps.title: Upload overnight and confirm on the dashboard
steps.who: The hub attendant, then two reviewers on the quality control team
steps.done: The dashboard shows that every phone going back has finished uploading. Two reviewers have given a decision on every video.
lines: The phones upload over the hub's fiber line through the night. One hour of footage is 5.4 GB. So one day of footage from a site takes hours to upload. This is why the phones cannot wait until the morning.
Before you release any phone, check on the dashboard that its uploads finished. A phone leaves the hub with no footage on it, or it does not leave.
Charge every phone while it uploads. Pack the phones again by site, with a new manifest. The manifest lists the device IDs, the count, the site, the time the case left, and the runner's name.

After the upload, two reviewers on the quality control team watch every video. If one of them says delete, the video is deleted. The video counts only when both reviewers accept it. Flags reach the Portfolio Manager the same day.

steps.title: Back on the chargers before 7:00 AM
steps.who: The runner, received by the senior operator
steps.done: Every cleared phone is on its charger in the device room before the operators clock in at 7:00 AM. Someone has signed for it.
lines: Take back only the phones the hub has cleared. The new manifest goes inside each case. Count the phones and compare the count with the manifest before you sign at the hub.
The same rules apply on the way back. Take one third of the phones per run. Use a locked case with no markings. Keep the letter in the bag. Never stop. Keep MDM tracking on.

At the site, the person who opens the device room counts the phones and compares the count with the manifest. That person signs, and you sign. Those two signatures are the custody record at the drop. Put every phone on a charger.
A phone that the hub held does not come back. It shows on the dashboard. The Portfolio Manager gives that wearer a spare phone today.
The runner finishes before 7:00 AM. The operators never wait for the phones.

steps.title: The next morning
steps.who: The operators, then the Portfolio Manager
steps.done: At 7:00 AM, the operators check the count, the batteries, the logins, and last night's upload again. The day starts over.
lines: At 7:00 AM, the day starts again. Open the room. Count the phones. Write the number. Check every battery and every login. Check that last night's upload finished.

Every flag from last night's review reaches the wearer within 24 hours. The wearer hears about it on the floor, with the video open. Three flags take the worker off the phone. A second strike pauses the phone until the worker is trained again.
